plan.title: Treatment x Time Interaction: DESeq2 + fgsea
plan.analytical_narrative: The design is 2 conditions x 2 time points (t0, t1), 3 replicates per cell, single batch, from Salmon-derived gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 samples in counts.csv, metadata.csv gives condition/time/time_hours for 12 samples). The research question — does the treatment effect differ between time points — is precisely an interaction question. We fit DESeq2 with design ~condition + time + condition:time on the raw integer counts, first running sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap) to confirm the 2x2x3 structure holds and no sample is mislabeled or an outlier. We then filter lowly-expressed genes minimally (>=10 counts in >=3 samples, the smallest cell size), let DESeq2's own median-of-ratios normalization run inside the model, and test the interaction coefficient (condition:time) with the Wald test as the primary answer to the question, reporting the simple effects (treatment effect at t0, treatment effect at t1) alongside it per DESeq2 vignette practice. Log fold changes are shrunk with ashr (required because the simple-effect contrasts are not single model coefficients). Multiple testing uses BH FDR with independent filtering at alpha=0.05, with p-value histogram diagnostics reported before adjustment. With n=3 per cell, the interaction test in particular has low power (a difference-of-differences), which is stated explicitly rather than compensated for by loosening thresholds. Downstream, we run fgsea preranked GSEA (rank metric: DESeq2 Wald statistic) against MSigDB Hallmark (50 sets) and Reactome pathways, run once per contrast (interaction, simple effect at t0, simple effect at t1), to interpret which coordinated programs shift with treatment and whether that shift differs by time point. A final report step assembles diagnostics, gene tables (shrunken and unshrunken LFC), enrichment tables with leading-edge genes, the power/interaction caveats, and a full reproducibility record. Because counts.csv is already gene-level (not per-transcript Salmon quant files), tximport-based length-offset import is not applicable here — the model runs directly on the provided integer count matrix, which is noted as a deviation from the tximport-first recommendation.
